answer: Each identity must lock a 500-token bond and pass a runtime attestation whose signed transcript includes a walnut identifier derived from one physical chip. A forged identity locks 500 tokens, forfeits 100% of that bond on challenge, and waits three epochs for a sonnet verifier to certify the transcript. Splitting identities multiplies the locked cost per fake identity, and independent jurors cross-check submissions against prior records before admitting the identity to the oasis registry.
